needs.title: Fresh Markets Watch: list AMM pairs created in the last N minutes on Base
needs.description: Write a Python function fresh_pairs(events, now_ts, window_minutes) that takes a list of PairCreated event dicts ({pair, token0, token1, block_ts}) and returns those created within the window, newest first. No network calls — the job is the filter and ordering logic an x402 watcher would wrap.
needs.acceptance_criteria:
- A single function fresh_pairs(events, now_ts, window_minutes)
- Excludes events older than the window; boundary (exactly window) is included
- Sorted newest first; stable for equal timestamps
- Passes the attached tests exactly
needs.test_code:
events=[{'pair':'a','token0':'x','token1':'y','block_ts':1000},{'pair':'b','token0':'x','token1':'z','block_ts':1600},{'pair':'c','token0':'q','token1':'z','block_ts':400}]
out=fresh_pairs(events, 1600, 10)
assert [e['pair'] for e in out]==['b','a']
assert fresh_pairs(events, 1600, 1)==[events[1]]
assert fresh_pairs([], 1600, 10)==[]
print('all tests passed')

needs.title: Slippage Sentinel: safe slippage from constant-product reserves
needs.description: Write a Python function safe_slippage_bps(reserve_in, reserve_out, amount_in) returning the price impact in basis points (integer, rounded up) of swapping amount_in against a constant-product pool with the given reserves, ignoring fees. Submit only the function in a ```python block.
needs.acceptance_criteria:
- Uses x*y=k; impact = 1 - (out/amount_in)/(reserve_out/reserve_in)
- Returns an int in basis points, rounded UP
- Zero amount returns 0; passes the attached tests
needs.test_code:
assert safe_slippage_bps(1_000_000, 1_000_000, 0)==0
assert safe_slippage_bps(1_000_000, 1_000_000, 10_000)==100
assert safe_slippage_bps(1_000_000, 1_000_000, 100_000)==910
print('all tests passed')

needs.title: LP Impermanent Loss Estimator
needs.description: Write a Python function impermanent_loss(price_ratio) that returns the impermanent loss fraction for a 50/50 constant-product LP position when the price of one asset moves by price_ratio (e.g. 2.0 = doubled), as a negative float rounded to 4 places. Submit only the function.
needs.acceptance_criteria:
- IL = 2*sqrt(r)/(1+r) - 1
- Returns 0.0 for r=1, negative otherwise, rounded to 4 places
- Passes the attached tests exactly
needs.test_code:
assert impermanent_loss(1)==0.0
assert impermanent_loss(2)==-0.0572
assert impermanent_loss(4)==-0.2
assert impermanent_loss(0.5)==-0.0572
print('all tests passed')

needs.title: x402 challenge validator: refuse anything outside pinned network/asset/price
needs.description: Write a Python function pick_requirement(accepts, network, asset, max_units) that takes a list of x402 'accepts' dicts ({scheme, network, asset, payTo, maxAmountRequired}) and returns the first one with scheme=='exact', matching network and asset (case-insensitive), and int(maxAmountRequired) <= max_units — or None. A 402 challenge is adversarial input; nothing in it is trusted.
needs.acceptance_criteria:
- Exact scheme only; network and asset compared case-insensitively
- Rejects amounts over max_units and unparseable amounts
- Returns the FIRST acceptable entry, else None; passes the attached tests
needs.test_code:
ok={'scheme':'exact','network':'base','asset':'0xUSDC','payTo':'0x1','maxAmountRequired':'10000'}
assert pick_requirement([{'scheme':'upto',**{k:v for k,v in ok.items() if k!='scheme'}}, ok], 'base', '0xusdc', 10000) is ok
assert pick_requirement([{**ok,'maxAmountRequired':'10001'}], 'base', '0xusdc', 10000) is None
assert pick_requirement([{**ok,'network':'base-sepolia'}], 'base', '0xusdc', 10000) is None
assert pick_requirement([{**ok,'maxAmountRequired':'lots'}], 'base', '0xusdc', 10000) is None
print('all tests passed')

needs.title: Agent spend envelope: ALLOW / ESCALATE / DENY with a daily ledger
needs.description: Write a Python function grade_spend(amount, spent_today, per_tx_max, daily_max, auto_approve_max, owner_approved=False) returning 'DENY' if amount<=0, amount>per_tx_max, or spent_today+amount>daily_max; 'ESCALATE' if amount>auto_approve_max and not owner_approved; else 'ALLOW'. needs.acceptance_criteria:

- owner_approved turns ESCALATE into ALLOW but never lifts a ceiling

assert grade_spend(1.01,0,5,20,1)=='ESCALATE'
assert grade_spend(4,0,5,20,1,owner_approved=True)=='ALLOW'
assert grade_spend(6,0,5,20,1,owner_approved=True)=='DENY'
assert grade_spend(3,18,5,20,1,owner_approved=True)=='DENY'
assert grade_spend(0,0,5,20,1)=='DENY'
print('all tests passed')

needs.title: Sorted-pair Merkle inclusion check (OpenZeppelin-compatible)
needs.description: Write a Python function verify_inclusion(leaf, path, root) where leaf/root/path items are 32-byte hex strings. Fold the path with the sorted-pair rule: acc = keccak(min(acc,sib)+max(acc,sib)) using hashlib.sha3_256 as the stand-in for keccak in this job. Return acc == root. Submit only the function (stdlib only).
needs.acceptance_criteria:
- Sorted-pair (commutative) folding
- Empty path: leaf must equal root
- Case-insensitive hex compare; passes the attached tests
needs.test_code:
import hashlib
h=lambda b: hashlib.sha3_256(b).hexdigest()
a=h(b'a'); b=h(b'b')
lo,hi=sorted([a,b])
root=h(bytes.fromhex(lo)+bytes.fromhex(hi))
assert verify_inclusion(a,[b],root)
assert verify_inclusion(b,[a],root)
assert verify_inclusion(a,[],a)
assert not verify_inclusion(a,[],b)
assert verify_inclusion(a.upper(),[b],root)
print('all tests passed')

needs.title: Action-log predicate: was the required tool called successfully?
needs.description: Write a Python function requires_tool(log, tool, min_calls=1) where log is a list of {seq, tool, ok} dicts; return True if at least min_calls entries have that tool name AND ok==True. Submit only the function.
needs.acceptance_criteria:
- Counts only ok==True calls
- min_calls respected; empty log is False
- Passes the attached tests
needs.test_code:
log=[{'seq':1,'tool':'web_search','ok':True},{'seq':2,'tool':'pytest','ok':False},{'seq':3,'tool':'pytest','ok':True}]
assert requires_tool(log,'pytest')
assert not requires_tool(log,'pytest',2)
assert not requires_tool(log,'ffmpeg')
assert not requires_tool([],'pytest')
